metadata.description: Comprehensive English grammar with coordination, prepositional phrases, and subordinate clauses

rules.note: Example: very quickly -> SPECIFIER(quickly) with child SPECIFIER(very)

adj1.description: Build descriptors with specifiers and subordinate clauses

mixPrep.description: Mix different prepositional types via coordination

noun1.description: Build nouns with descriptors and subordinate clauses

rules.note: Example: cats and dogs -> COORD becomes NOUN
Example: on table and under chair

Infinitive: to run, to see (anchor becomes NOMINAL result). Scoped to INFINITIVE (round 2): without it, any MODIFIER (e.g. a modal like "can") immediately before an already-VERBAL node was wrongly read as an infinitive marker, stealing SUBJECT binding in modal+passive chains like "can be found".
Gerund as nominal: running is fun (PARTICIPLE → NOMINAL)
Participle as adjective: running water (PARTICIPLE → DESCRIPTOR)

Negation: not run, n't go. Scoped to NEGATIVE (round 2): without it, any MODIFIER (e.g. "be"/"is") immediately before a VERBAL was wrongly consumed as if it were a negation particle, pre-empting aux1 for modal+passive chains like "can be found".

rel1.description: Relative clauses with pronouns (fires before clause1 so the relative pronoun is still unconsumed)

rules.note: Relative clause: the dog who chased (anchor->PREDICATE, PREDICATE->who)

Object-relative clause: the ball that mary found (gap after the verb -- the relative marker is not the embedded subject, so the intervening NOMINAL is; anchor stays NOMINAL so it can still become the matrix clause's own subject)

rel2.description: Relative clauses with adverbs (fires before clause1)

rules.note: Relative adverb: the place where I live

noun4.description: Noun-noun apposition (placed after rel1/rel2 so relative pronouns are not consumed first)

rules.note: Noun-noun apposition (late-binding, after relative clause rules)

aux1.description: Auxiliary verbs modify main verbs (modals, perfect, progressive, passive)

rules.note: Passive voice: be + past participle (mary can be found). Anchor is the participle (not "be") so push_subtypes lands on the node that survives the aux1 chain; SUBJECT still comes from the generic clause1 rule (preverbal NOMINAL -> SUBJECT), so no ConnectionType change is needed downstream.
Modal + verb: can run, should go
Perfect auxiliary + verb: has run, had eaten
Progressive auxiliary + verb: is running, was walking
Bare progressive copula -> VERBAL (e.g. 'is' in 'mary is in the kitchen')
Example: dog runs and cat sleeps

verb1b.description: Second-pass: attach subordinate clauses to already-formed CLAUSEs (matrix verbs)

rules.note: Second pass: [john said] + [that he left](SUBORDINATE) -> CLAUSE

predicate1b.description: Second-pass placeholder (no-op; kept for order consistency)
